The IFN / antiviral rows show that interferon-response genes are concentrated in stimulation-linked patterns. In the selected R run, the IFN-associated pattern, `Pattern4`, has 16 of the 17 targeted IFN / antiviral genes among its top 50 genes. `Pattern5` also has strong IFN / antiviral gene support, which is why it was described earlier as monocyte-biased stimulation-linked rather than ignored. This is a useful reminder that gene-set support does not name a pattern by itself. The broader interpretation still depends on the activity evidence: `Pattern4` is the broad IFN-associated pattern because it combines IFN-linked genes with the strongest stimulation correlation and paired donor shift.

The antigen-presentation rows give a different kind of evidence. In the selected R run, `Pattern3` has the strongest antigen-presentation support, with 8 of the 10 targeted antigen-presentation genes among its top 50 genes. The overlapping genes include `CD74` and HLA class II genes such as `HLA-DRA`, `HLA-DRB1`, `HLA-DPA1`, and `HLA-DPB1`. That result supports using `Pattern3` as a contrast pattern: it looks less like a broad IFN-beta stimulation response and more like dendritic-cell / antigen-presentation-linked structure.

The main takeaway is not that one p-value settles the biology. Instead, the targeted gene-set check adds a second layer of evidence to the earlier activity summaries. It shows that the model contains both interferon-response gene structure and non-IFN immune structure, which is exactly what you need if the goal is to separate stimulation-associated activity from cell-type-linked biology.

### Use An Identity-Linked Pattern As A Contrast

It is tempting to focus only on the IFN-associated pattern, but that would miss an important lesson. A good latent-variable analysis should also ask what the other patterns capture. The targeted gene-set check above points to an antigen-presentation-linked pattern whose top genes include `CD74` and HLA class II genes. This pattern is useful as a contrast because it looks more like immune-cell identity or antigen-presentation structure than a broad stimulation response.

The code below selects the pattern with the strongest antigen-presentation targeted enrichment and summarizes its top genes and direction. This gives you a second example of why CoGAPS gene weights and expression direction should be interpreted together.

The selection step uses the targeted gene-set table you just created. It keeps only the rows for the antigen-presentation gene set, sorts those rows by enrichment p-value, and takes the top row. That top row gives the pattern whose highest-weight genes are most enriched for the targeted antigen-presentation markers. After that, the code goes back to the directionality table, keeps only genes from that selected pattern, sorts them by CoGAPS gene-weight rank, and prints the first 12 genes.

In the R tab, `filter()` keeps the antigen-presentation rows, `arrange()` puts the smallest p-value first, `slice(1)` keeps the strongest row, and `pull(pattern)` extracts the pattern label as a single value. The next pipe uses that label to filter `direction_global_r`, then formats the log2 fold-change and pair-consistency columns for display. That matters because PBMC data contain immune-cell identity structure before any stimulation comparison is made. This contrast also protects the IFN interpretation from becoming too broad. The IFN-associated pattern is supported by a stimulation shift, an ISG-score correlation, and IFN / antiviral top genes. ### Question 2 Answer: Broad Stimulation And Identity-Linked Structure Are Both Present

Question 2 asked whether CoGAPS can help distinguish broad stimulation-associated activity from cell-type-linked immune programs. The evidence in this section supports a cautious yes.

The paired donor test showed that the IFN-associated pattern is higher after IFN-beta stimulation in all eight matched donor pairs. The mixed model reached the same conclusion while accounting for donor baselines. The ISG-score check showed that cells with higher IFN-associated CoGAPS activity also tend to have higher expression of a compact interferon-stimulated gene score. The targeted gene-set check then connected the same pattern to IFN / antiviral genes among its highest-weight genes.

The contrast pattern adds the other half of the answer. The model does not only contain a stimulation signal. It also contains a pattern whose evidence points toward dendritic-cell / antigen-presentation-linked biology. That is important because the PBMC mixture is not a blank background. It contains immune-cell identities, and a useful latent-variable model should preserve some of that structure rather than forcing every signal to be interpreted as stimulation.

Together, these checks show why the case study does not rely on one diagnostic alone. A stimulation-associated pattern should be active in the expected cells, shift in the expected condition, agree with known interferon biology, and have genes that support the interpretation. A cell-identity-linked pattern should have a different evidence profile. With that distinction in place, the next question turns from where the IFN-associated pattern is active to which genes define it and whether those genes rise or fall after stimulation.

## Question 3: Which Genes Define The IFN-Associated Pattern, And In Which Direction?

This question asks which genes make the IFN-associated pattern interpretable and whether those genes are higher or lower after stimulation. That distinction matters because CoGAPS gene weights identify genes that define a pattern, while expression contrasts identify direction.

### Inspect Direction Within The IFN-Associated Pattern

Now return to the key point from the visualization section: CoGAPS weights and expression direction are different quantities. A high gene weight means the gene helps define the pattern. {{< glossary "Directionality" display="Directionality" >}} asks whether the gene is higher or lower after IFN-beta stimulation.

The table below focuses on the top genes from the IFN-associated pattern. It shows their CoGAPS weight alongside a donor-aware {{< glossary "Pseudobulk" display="pseudobulk" >}} log2 fold-change. Pseudobulk means that the single-cell counts are first added up within a meaningful group, such as one donor's control cells or the same donor's stimulated cells, before conditions are compared. That keeps the paired donor design visible and avoids treating thousands of cells from the same donor as thousands of independent donors.

The directionality summaries were generated before this section from the saved selected-model outputs and the count layer in the prepared PBMC dataset. The workflow did five things:

1. extracted the top genes for each CoGAPS pattern from the gene-weight matrix,
2. aggregated raw counts for those genes by donor and condition,
3. converted each pseudobulk profile to counts per million, or CPM, so groups with different total counts are more comparable,
4. computed `log2(stimulated CPM + 0.5) - log2(control CPM + 0.5)` for each donor pair, and
5. summarized the mean direction, pair consistency, and adjusted Wilcoxon evidence for each pattern gene.

The `+ 0.5` term is a small pseudocount. It prevents zeros from causing undefined logarithms. A positive mean log2 fold-change means the gene is higher after IFN-beta stimulation; a negative value means it is lower after stimulation.

Here is how to read the table. **Rank** orders genes by their CoGAPS weight within the IFN-associated pattern. **CoGAPS weight** tells you how strongly each gene helps define that pattern. **Mean log2FC: IFN-beta vs control** is the donor-aware expression contrast from the pseudobulk analysis. **Direction** translates the sign of that contrast into a readable label. **Pair consistency** tells you how often donor pairs agree in direction; a value of `1.00` means every usable donor pair moved in the same direction. **FDR** is the Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted Wilcoxon result from this targeted paired summary.

The main result is clear in both implementations: 14 of the top 15 IFN-associated pattern genes are higher after IFN-beta stimulation. Many of those genes, including `ISG15`, `IFI6`, `IFIT3`, `IFIT1`, `MX1`, `OAS1`, and `BST2`, are familiar interferon-stimulated genes, so the direction of change supports the IFN-associated interpretation. The one exception among the top 15 is `FTH1`, which has a high pattern weight but is lower after stimulation in this targeted summary.

That exception is important rather than problematic. It shows why the analysis keeps gene weight and expression direction separate. CoGAPS says that `FTH1` helps define the pattern; the pseudobulk contrast says that its expression moves opposite the main ISG group after stimulation. A careful interpretation therefore describes the IFN-associated pattern as dominated by up-shifted interferon-stimulated genes, while noting that not every high-weight gene is up-regulated.

## Question 4: How Does The IFN-Associated Pattern Vary Across PBMC Identities?

This question asks whether the IFN-associated signal is broad across the PBMC mixture or mostly driven by one annotated immune-cell identity. The next check keeps the same IFN-associated top genes but summarizes their stimulation direction inside each annotated PBMC identity.

### Check Whether The Direction Holds Across PBMC Identities

The IFN-associated pattern is broad, but PBMCs are a mixture of immune-cell identities. A responsible analysis asks whether the same direction appears across those identities or whether the global result is driven by one large cell type.

The next summary counts, within each annotated PBMC identity, how many of the IFN-associated pattern's top genes are higher in stimulation, lower in stimulation, or mixed/unclear. The code uses `group_by()` and `summarise()` in R, and `groupby()` with `size()` in Python. These methods are common data-analysis skills: they split a table into groups, compute a summary inside each group, and return a smaller table.

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### R


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
  dplyr::filter(pattern == ifn_pattern_r) |>
  dplyr::group_by(cell_type, direction) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n_genes = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(
```

## Pull The Evidence Together

The four main research questions are now connected to specific evidence. The table below makes that map explicit before the final synthesis.

| Main research question | Evidence used in this section | Current answer |
|---|---|---|
| **1. What latent transcriptional programs are present?** | R/Python pattern matching, candidate-program inventory, targeted gene-set checks, and identity-linked contrast. | The selected model contains a strong IFN-associated pattern plus additional immune-cell-linked structure, including antigen-presentation-linked biology. |
| **2. Can CoGAPS distinguish broad stimulation-associated activity from cell-type-linked immune programs?** | Donor-paired IFN activity shift, donor-adjusted mixed-model check, canonical ISG-score agreement, IFN/antiviral enrichment, antigen-presentation enrichment, and identity-linked contrast. | Yes, the evidence supports a broad stimulation-associated signal while retaining non-IFN immune structure. |
| **3. Which genes define the strongest IFN-associated pattern, and what is their direction in stimulation?** | IFN-associated gene weights paired with donor-aware pseudobulk directionality. | Top genes such as `ISG15`, `IFI6`, `IFIT3`, `IFIT1`, `MX1`, `OAS1`, and `BST2` define the pattern and are mostly higher after IFN-beta stimulation. |
| **4. How does the IFN-associated pattern vary across annotated PBMC cell types?** | Cell-type-stratified direction summaries for the IFN-associated pattern's top genes. | The IFN-associated direction is broadly visible across annotated PBMC identities, with room for differences in response strength across cell types. |

Taken together, these checks support a coherent interpretation rather than a single-metric label. The selected R model has enough diagnostic support to interpret cautiously: the chi-square trace reaches a plateau-like region, the snapshot checks show stable top genes for the major patterns, and the posterior uncertainty summaries do not suggest that the IFN-associated pattern is too unstable to use. Those checks do not prove that `K = 6` is universally best. They do support using this selected model to ask the biological questions posed in the case study.

The first answer is that the model contains more than one kind of latent structure. The IFN-associated pattern is the clearest stimulation-linked signal: in the selected R run it is `Pattern4`, and in the Python saved output it is `Pattern5`. The number changes because CoGAPS pattern labels are run-specific, but the evidence points to the same biological signal: high activity after IFN-beta stimulation, high agreement with an interferon-stimulated gene score, and top genes such as `ISG15`, `IFI6`, `IFIT3`, `IFIT1`, `MX1`, `OAS1`, and `BST2`. The model also retains immune-cell-linked patterns, including monocyte-linked structure, a dendritic / antigen-presentation-linked pattern, and a T-cell / lymphocyte-linked baseline pattern. That matters because the analysis is not simply rediscovering "stimulated versus control"; it is separating stimulation-associated activity from other structure already present in the PBMC mixture.

The second answer is that the stimulation-associated signal is broad, but not identical in every cell type. The donor-paired analysis shows higher IFN-associated activity after stimulation in all eight matched donor pairs, and the mixed model reaches the same conclusion while accounting for donor baselines. The visualization section prepared the same idea visually: the UMAP activity maps showed that this pattern cuts across the cell-identity map rather than sitting in only one neighborhood. The cell-type-stratified summaries then showed that annotated PBMC identities can share the IFN-associated direction while still differing in response strength. This is the useful middle ground for a mixed immune-cell dataset: a shared perturbation response can be visible without erasing cell identity.

The third answer is that CoGAPS gene weights and expression direction have to be read together. The top genes for the IFN-associated pattern are strongly consistent with interferon biology, but the weights alone only say that those genes help define the pattern. The pseudobulk directionality summaries add the missing piece: among the top IFN-associated genes, most are higher after IFN-beta stimulation, while an exception such as `FTH1` shows why direction cannot be assumed from the CoGAPS weight. The identity-linked contrast reinforces the same lesson. A dendritic / antigen-presentation-linked pattern can be defined by genes such as `CD74` and HLA class II genes without behaving like the broad IFN-associated stimulation pattern.

The fourth answer is that the IFN-associated pattern varies across annotated PBMC identities in a biologically interpretable way. PBMCs contain T cells, B cells, NK cells, monocytes, dendritic cells, and smaller related populations. The lupus and interferon literature discussed in the context section makes this mixture important: type I interferon biology can connect multiple immune-cell populations through interferon-stimulated genes, antigen presentation, monocyte and dendritic-cell activity, and lymphocyte responses. In this dataset, the controlled IFN-beta stimulation lets you see one part of that biology under an experimental perturbation. The CoGAPS result is consistent with a shared interferon-response program layered on top of immune-cell identity.

The conclusion is therefore bounded but useful. For this public PBMC perturbation dataset from lupus donors, the selected R `K = 6` sparse CoGAPS model is suitable for interpreting the main case-study question. It recovers a broad IFN-beta-associated pattern, preserves additional immune-cell-linked structure, and links the IFN-associated pattern to both expected interferon-stimulated genes and upward expression direction after stimulation. The result should not be read as a clinical lupus mechanism, a treatment analysis, or proof that the same numbered pattern will appear in every run. It does show that latent-pattern analysis can help separate a shared interferon-response signal from cell identity in a mixed immune-cell system, which is the key analysis skill this case study is designed to teach.

# **Summary**
***

## **Synopsis**
***

In this case study, we used a processed PBMC single-cell RNA-seq dataset with control and IFN-beta stimulated cells to learn how a latent-variable method can reveal transcriptional programs that cut across cell-type labels.

We inspected the processed single-cell object, summarized condition and cell-type metadata, prepared a genes x cells CoGAPS input, and loaded selected R-primary CoGAPS artifacts. The rank `K = 6` was selected before the main learner workflow using a limited model-selection sweep and follow-up pattern-structure comparison. Learners do not need to run that sweep to complete the case study.

The strongest stimulation-associated program in the selected R K6 model is the IFN-associated pattern, labeled `Pattern4` in that run. It is anchored by canonical interferon-stimulated genes, including `ISG15`, `ISG20`, `IFI6`, `IFIT3`, `IFIT1`, `MX1`, `IFIT2`, `IRF7`, `OAS1`, `PLSCR1`, and `BST2`.

We also performed a targeted directionality check because CoGAPS pattern weights do not by themselves indicate whether genes are up or down in stimulation. In the selected R K6 analysis, 14 of the top 15 IFN-associated pattern genes were up in IFN-beta stimulation, while `FTH1` was down.

The IFN-associated pattern activity appears broad across PBMC cell types, supporting an activity-like IFN-response interpretation. Other patterns have interpretable gene anchors, such as myeloid and antigen-presentation genes, but those secondary interpretations should remain more cautious.

Make a compact table or bar plot showing each gene's {{< glossary "Gene weight" display="CoGAPS weight" >}} and {{< glossary "Directionality" display="directionality" >}} after IFN-beta stimulation. ## Reproduction Roadmap

## Stage 2: Rebuild The Prepared PBMC Dataset

Use this stage when you want to reconstruct the expression dataset that CoGAPS received. The source file contains the larger single-cell count dataset; the prepared file keeps the cells, metadata, normalized expression values, and 3,000 highly variable genes used in the analysis.

```text
data/processed/input/preprocessed_cells_hvg3000.h5ad
```

If you already have the included prepared file and do not want to revisit preprocessing, you can continue to Stage 3. Reading the explanation is still useful because filtering, normalization, transformation, and gene selection determine the exact matrix available to the model.

The preprocessing script is:

```text
scripts/reproduction/prepare_preprocessed_hvg3000.py
```

It performs six main jobs:

1. reads the larger source `.h5ad` file;
1. keeps a raw count layer for steps that need count-scale values;
1. removes genes detected in too few cells;
1. normalizes and log-transforms expression values;
1. selects 3,000 highly variable genes; and
1. writes both the prepared case-study data file and the optional dense PyCoGAPS input.

The recorded preprocessing workflow is implemented in Python. Run the complete script inside Docker from `/home/rstudio/project` after the source file is available:

```bash
/opt/cogaps-venv/bin/python scripts/reproduction/prepare_preprocessed_hvg3000.py \
  --source-h5ad data/source/kang_counts_25k.h5ad \
  --out-h5ad data/processed/input/preprocessed_cells_hvg3000.h5ad \
  --cogaps-input-h5ad data/processed/input/cogaps_input_genesxcells_hvg3000_float64.h5ad \
  --config-json data/processed/input/preprocess_config_hvg3000.json
```

### The Script Starts By Making The Choices Visible

The first important design choice is that preprocessing settings are command-line arguments, not hidden constants. The script has defaults, but the command above could override them if you wanted to test another preprocessing recipe.

```python
parser.add_argument("--min-cells", type=int, default=3)
parser.add_argument("--target-sum", type=float, default=10000.0)
parser.add_argument("--n-top-genes", type=int, default=3000)
parser.add_argument("--hvg-flavor", default="seurat_v3")
```

These four arguments describe the main preprocessing decisions:

- `min_cells = 3` means a gene must be detected in at least three cells to remain in the dataset.
- `target_sum = 10000` means each cell is rescaled to the same total expression depth before log transformation.
- `n_top_genes = 3000` means the prepared CoGAPS input uses 3,000 highly variable genes.
- `hvg_flavor = "seurat_v3"` names the highly variable gene-selection method.

This is a useful reproducibility habit. If a later model result changes, you can check whether the model changed or whether the expression matrix was rebuilt with different preprocessing settings.

### The Script Reads The Source AnnData File And Preserves Counts

The source file is an AnnData `.h5ad` object. In single-cell analysis, an AnnData object usually stores cells as rows and genes as columns. The main expression matrix is `adata.X`, and additional versions of the matrix can be stored in `adata.layers`.

The script reads the source file and makes sure there is a `counts` layer:

```python
adata = ad.read_h5ad(args.source_h5ad)

if "counts" not in adata.layers:
    adata.layers["counts"] = adata.X.copy()
```

This matters because the workflow uses expression values in more than one way. The normalized, log-transformed matrix is easier to compare across cells and is the matrix used for the prepared case-study file. The count-scale layer is kept so highly variable gene selection can use count-like values, and so later full-reproduction steps have a clear record of where count-scale information came from.

### Filtering Removes Genes With Too Little Information

The first filtering step removes genes detected in too few cells:

```python
sc.pp.filter_genes(adata, min_cells=args.min_cells)
```

This step does not decide which immune cells are important. It only removes genes that are so rarely detected that they are unlikely to help the factorization. In this workflow, a gene must be detected in at least three cells. That low threshold is intentionally permissive: it removes nearly absent genes while retaining a broad expression space for the highly variable gene step.

### Normalization And Log Transformation Put Cells On A Comparable Scale

Single cells can differ in total captured RNA or sequencing depth. Before comparing expression values across cells, the script rescales each cell and then log-transforms the normalized values:

```python
sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum=args.target_sum)
sc.pp.log1p(adata)
```

`normalize_total()` rescales each cell so that its total expression is comparable to the same target value. Here, that target is 10,000. `log1p()` then applies a log transform using `log(1 + expression)`, which reduces the dominance of very large expression values while keeping zeros defined.

For this case study, the important point is not the specific number 10,000 by itself. The important point is that CoGAPS receives an expression matrix where cells have already been put on a more comparable scale.

### Highly Variable Genes Define The Modeling Space

The source study measured many genes, but the selected model uses 3,000 highly variable genes. Highly variable genes are genes whose expression varies enough across cells to help distinguish cell states, cell identities, stimulation responses, or other structure.

The script marks highly variable genes, then creates a reduced AnnData object:

```python
sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(
    adata,
    n_top_genes=args.n_top_genes,
    flavor=args.hvg_flavor,
    layer="counts",
    subset=False,
)

adata_hvg = adata[:, adata.var["highly_variable"].to_numpy()].copy()
```

There are two small programming details worth noticing here. First, `subset=False` means the function adds a `highly_variable` column to `adata.var` rather than immediately dropping genes. Second, the next line uses that Boolean column as a mask to keep only the selected genes. A Boolean mask is a true/false vector: genes marked `TRUE` stay in `adata_hvg`, and genes marked `FALSE` are left behind.

The result is the prepared matrix used by the case study:

```text
24,673 cells x 3,000 highly variable genes
```

### The Script Writes Two Orientations Of The Same Prepared Data

The main prepared file is written as cells by genes, which is the usual AnnData orientation:

```python
adata_hvg.write_h5ad(args.out_h5ad)
```

The script also creates an optional dense genes-by-cells file for the Python/PyCoGAPS full rerun:

```python
def build_cogaps_input(preprocessed_cells: ad.AnnData) -> ad.AnnData:
    cogaps_input = preprocessed_cells.T.copy()
    X = cogaps_input.X.toarray() if sparse.issparse(cogaps_input.X) else cogaps_input.X
    cogaps_input.X = np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
    cogaps_input.var = preprocessed_cells.obs.copy()
    cogaps_input.var_names = preprocessed_cells.obs_names.astype(str).copy()
    cogaps_input.obs = preprocessed_cells.var.copy()
    cogaps_input.obs_names = preprocessed_cells.var_names.astype(str).copy()
    return cogaps_input
```

This function transposes the matrix so genes become rows and cells become columns. It also densifies the matrix and stores it as `float64`. That dense genes-by-cells file is not needed for the main analysis, but it is needed if you want to rerun the Python-compatible CoGAPS workflow with the supplied launcher.

The two outputs are therefore different views of the same prepared expression space:

- `preprocessed_cells_hvg3000.h5ad`: cells by genes, used for the main analysis and most summaries.
- `cogaps_input_genesxcells_hvg3000_float64.h5ad`: genes by cells, used for the optional full Python-compatible rerun.

### Record The Preprocessing Choices

At the end, the script writes a compact JSON record:

```python
config = {
    "raw_h5ad": args.source_h5ad.name,
    "min_cells": args.min_cells,
    "target_sum": args.target_sum,
    "hvg_flavor": args.hvg_flavor,
    "n_top_genes": args.n_top_genes,
    "prepared_h5ad": str(args.out_h5ad),
    "cogaps_input_h5ad": str(args.cogaps_input_h5ad),
}
args.config_json.write_text(json.dumps(config, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
```

After the script finishes, inspect `data/processed/input/preprocess_config_hvg3000.json`. That record should name the source file, minimum cell threshold, library-size target, highly variable gene method, number of selected genes, and output paths.

This file records the expression space given to CoGAPS before model interpretation begins. It answers questions such as why the selected model has 3,000 genes and whether the expression matrix was normalized before model fitting.

## Stage 3: Fit The Selected R CoGAPS Model

The selected R model is the primary fitted model used in the analysis. This stage runs CoGAPS and saves the complete model object. ### Run The Model Where You Can See Its Progress

Run the launcher from your normal computer Terminal or from the Docker/RStudio Terminal while you can watch the output:

```bash
bash scripts/reproduction/run_selected_model_r.sh
```

The launcher writes selected-model outputs to:

```text
data/processed/selected_model_k6/r/
```

If a full R selected-model object already exists, the launcher stops before overwriting it. To intentionally rerun the model, set `FORCE_RERUN=1`:

```bash
FORCE_RERUN=1 bash scripts/reproduction/run_selected_model_r.sh
```

The launcher checks that R CoGAPS was compiled with OpenMP support and sets `OMP_NUM_THREADS=4` before starting the run. It then calls `scripts/cogaps_run_one_singleprocess_r.R` with the selected settings.

The R runner does four important things:

1. reads `data/processed/input/preprocessed_cells_hvg3000.h5ad` with `zellkonverter`;
1. extracts the normalized expression matrix used by CoGAPS;
1. builds `CogapsParams()` with the selected `K`, seed, iteration count, and sparse-optimization setting; and
1. saves the full CoGAPS result as `cogaps_K6_seed2_iter2000.rds`.

The log should show CoGAPS progressing through equilibration and sampling. During **equilibration**, the sampler moves away from its starting state and toward a region of the model space that fits the data better. During **sampling**, CoGAPS continues updating the model while collecting the posterior summaries used in the final result.

While the run is active, check for four signs of progress:

1. the input dimensions and selected settings are printed correctly;
1. iteration numbers continue to increase;
1. the run moves from equilibration into sampling; and
1. the final requested sampling iteration is reached without an error.

Chi-square values do not need to decrease at every sampling update. CoGAPS is a stochastic sampler rather than a monotone optimizer, so small fluctuations during the sampling phase are expected. The diagnostic exports in Stage 4 make the full trace easier to inspect.

The first files to check after this stage are the full selected R CoGAPS object, the metrics JSON, and the checkpoint file. The `.rds` object is the source for later exports. The metrics JSON provides a compact record of settings, runtime, dimensions, and headline model summaries. The checkpoint is mainly useful for debugging or resuming a run.

**Stage 3 checkpoint:** The Terminal shows that equilibration and sampling completed, and `data/processed/selected_model_k6/r/` contains the full `.rds` model and metrics JSON. Do not continue to the export stage if the fit ended with an error or stopped before completing sampling.

## Stage 4: Create Diagnostic And Analysis Tables

The full model object contains much more information than is practical to display directly in a web page. This stage creates smaller files for two purposes:

- **diagnostic tables** summarize the model trace, snapshots, assignments, and posterior uncertainty;
- **analysis tables** organize gene weights, cell activities, top genes, and grouped activity summaries into forms that can be inspected with R or Python.

These are not additional model fits. They are different views of the same selected R result.

## Stage 6: Confirm The Reproduction

A successful script exit is necessary, but it is not the only check. Confirm that the regenerated files still represent the intended dataset and model.

| Check | Expected result | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Prepared data | 24,673 cells, 3,000 genes, and the required condition, donor, cell-type, and UMAP fields | Confirms that CoGAPS received the intended cells, genes, and metadata. |
| Selected settings | `K = 6`, seed 2, 2,000 iterations per phase, and sparse optimization enabled | Confirms that the regenerated model matches the selected specification. |
| Pattern structure | Six gene-weight and cell-activity columns with aligned pattern labels | Confirms that the compact exports describe the complete selected model. |
| Diagnostics | Trace, snapshot, uncertainty, metrics, and available pump files are present for R | Confirms that the evidence needed to evaluate the R run was exported. |
| Directionality | Global, cell-type, paired, and pseudobulk support tables are present | Confirms that expression direction can be interpreted separately from CoGAPS weights. |
| Display files | Figures were rebuilt after their source tables | Confirms that the page displays the current evidence. |

## Optional Extension: Understand How The Rank Sweep Was Run

The full rank sweep supports the choice of `K = 6`, but it is not part of local reproduction. The sweep used many CoGAPS runs across candidate ranks, seeds, and iteration counts. That is cluster work, not work you need to do on a local computer.

The useful idea is not the exact cluster command. The useful idea is the design pattern: build one reproducible input, write an explicit table of model runs, let the scheduler run one row at a time, and aggregate the completed runs into evidence tables before choosing one model for interpretation.

The included model-selection summaries live under:

```text
data/processed/k_selection/
```

Those files are used in [Data Import](#data-import) to evaluate model resolution. They connect the completed sweep runs with the model-choice tables shown in the case study.

For transparency, the repository includes portable copies of the scripts that prepared the sweep inputs, ran individual model fits, aggregated completed runs, and summarized candidate models:


### Initial Sweep Order

The first sweep pass used the same cached PBMC input for all model runs. That matters because the rank comparison should not mix changes in `K` with changes in preprocessing. The preparation job therefore runs once before the array is submitted.

```bash
# Stage 1: build the cached PBMC input and the jobs table.
sbatch prep_cogaps_cache_and_jobs_rhino_light.sbatch
```

The preparation job calls these two Python programs:

```bash
python3 cogaps_prep_cache.py \
  --input-h5ad kang_counts_25k.h5ad \
  --outdir results_cogaps_singleprocess_hpc \
  --min-cells 3 \
  --target-sum 10000 \
  --n-top-genes 3000 \
  --hvg-flavor seurat_v3

python3 make_cogaps_jobs_tsv.py \
  --k-grid 7,9,11,13 \
  --seeds 1,2,3,4,5 \
  --iters 2000,10000,20000 \
  --out results_cogaps_singleprocess_hpc/jobs.tsv
```

The jobs table is intentionally simple. It has no header; each line is a tab-separated `K`, seed, and iteration count. The initial sweep table had `60` rows: four candidate ranks, five seeds, and three iteration settings.

```bash
# Stage 2: submit one Slurm array task per row in jobs.tsv.
OUTDIR=results_cogaps_singleprocess_hpc
JOBS_TSV=${OUTDIR}/jobs.tsv
N=$(wc -l < "${JOBS_TSV}")

sbatch --export=ALL,OUTDIR="${OUTDIR}",JOBS_TSV="${JOBS_TSV}" \
  --array=0-$((N-1))%15 \
  cogaps_sweep_array_singleprocess_rhino_light.sbatch
```

The `%15` limit is a concurrency cap. It allows at most 15 array tasks to run at the same time. Each task is still one single-process CoGAPS run; the cluster parallelism comes from running many independent rows of the jobs table.

Each array task reads one row from `jobs.tsv` and calls:

```bash
python3 cogaps_run_one_singleprocess.py \
  --cogaps-input-h5ad results_cogaps_singleprocess_hpc/cache/cogaps_input_genesxcells_hvg3000_float64.h5ad \
  --outdir results_cogaps_singleprocess_hpc \
  --k "${K}" \
  --seed "${SEED}" \
  --n-iter "${NITER}" \
  --stim-label "stim" \
  --top-genes 50 \
  --use-sparse-opt \
  --blas-threads "${NTHREADS}" \
  --cogaps-threads "${NTHREADS}"
```

That single-run script writes one saved result and one metrics JSON for the row it received. The metrics file is important because it records the runtime, selected IFN-associated pattern, IFN correlation, top genes, and status for that model.

```bash
# Stage 3: aggregate after the array completes.
sbatch --dependency=afterok:<ARRAY_JOB_ID> \
  aggregate_cogaps_results_rhino_light.sbatch
```

After the model jobs finish, the aggregation job calls:

```bash
python3 cogaps_aggregate_results.py \
  --outdir results_cogaps_singleprocess_hpc \
  --k-grid 7,9,11,13 \
  --seeds 1,2,3,4,5 \
  --iters 2000,10000,20000 \
  --top-genes 50 \
  --preprocessed-h5ad results_cogaps_singleprocess_hpc/cache/preprocessed_cells_hvg3000.h5ad \
  --no-umap
```

Aggregation is where individual model runs become model-selection evidence. The script does not choose a model by looking at one run in isolation. It reads the available metrics files, checks whether expected combinations are missing, summarizes performance by candidate rank, and writes the tables that can be inspected in the case study.

### High-K Extension

The high-rank extension asked the opposite question: could much larger ranks reveal useful structure that the lower-rank candidates missed? It used candidate values from `K = 14` to `K = 80` at 2,000 iterations:

```bash
bash submit_phase3_highk_2000_rhino.sh
```

That helper prepares the high-K jobs table, makes the Slurm launch files available on Rhino, submits the array, and then submits the aggregation job after the array succeeds. The same single-run Python script performs the model fit for each row.

The high-K jobs table used:

```text
K_GRID=14,20,26,32,38,44,50,56,62,68,74,80
SEEDS=1,2,3,4,5
ITERS=2000
```

After those runs, `phase3_highk_fragmentation_analysis.py` summarized whether high ranks improved the IFN-associated evidence or mostly split signal across extra patterns. The current model decision uses the high-K extension as a check against missing a clearly better high-rank model; it does not make high-K reruns part of local reproduction.

````{.r code-copy="true"}
top_genes_from_matrix_r <- function(matrix, pattern, n = 15) {
  ordered <- sort(matrix[, pattern], decreasing = TRUE)
  ordered <- head(ordered, n)
  tibble::tibble(
    gene = names(ordered),
    weight = unname(ordered)
  )
}

load_lightweight_pattern_matrices_r <- function(weights_path, activities_path) {
  A <- readr::read_tsv(weights_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    tibble::column_to_rownames("gene") |>
    as.data.frame(check.names = FALSE)
  P <- readr::read_tsv(activities_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    tibble::column_to_rownames("cell_barcode") |>
    as.data.frame(check.names = FALSE)
  colnames(A) <- canonicalize_pattern_names_r(colnames(A))
  colnames(P) <- canonicalize_pattern_names_r(colnames(P))
  list(A = A, P = P)
}
````

````{.python code-copy="true"}
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Recreate the prepared PBMC dataset from a larger source H5AD file.

This script is for the optional full reproduction path. The main learner path
uses the prepared H5AD and lightweight CoGAPS outputs already included with the
case study.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import anndata as ad
import numpy as np
from scipy import sparse


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--source-h5ad",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("data/source/kang_counts_25k.h5ad"),
        help="Larger source counts H5AD file.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--out-h5ad",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("data/processed/input/preprocessed_cells_hvg3000.h5ad"),
        help="Prepared cells x genes H5AD file.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--cogaps-input-h5ad",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("data/processed/input/cogaps_input_genesxcells_hvg3000_float64.h5ad"),
        help="Optional dense genes x cells PyCoGAPS input.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--config-json",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("data/processed/input/preprocess_config_hvg3000.json"),
        help="Preprocessing settings record.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--min-cells", type=int, default=3)
    parser.add_argument("--target-sum", type=float, default=10000.0)
    parser.add_argument("--n-top-genes", type=int, default=3000)
    parser.add_argument("--hvg-flavor", default="seurat_v3")
    return parser.parse_args()


def build_cogaps_input(preprocessed_cells: ad.AnnData) -> ad.AnnData:
    """Convert cells x genes AnnData into a dense genes x cells file."""
    cogaps_input = preprocessed_cells.T.copy()
    X = cogaps_input.X.toarray() if sparse.issparse(cogaps_input.X) else cogaps_input.X
    cogaps_input.X = np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
    cogaps_input.var = preprocessed_cells.obs.copy()
    cogaps_input.var_names = preprocessed_cells.obs_names.astype(str).copy()
    cogaps_input.obs = preprocessed_cells.var.copy()
    cogaps_input.obs_names = preprocessed_cells.var_names.astype(str).copy()
    return cogaps_input


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()

    try:
        import scanpy as sc
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise SystemExit(
            "This full-reproduction preprocessing script requires scanpy. "
            "Use the validated case-study image or install scanpy in your environment."
        ) from exc

    if not args.source_h5ad.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"Source H5AD not found: {args.source_h5ad}. "
            "Download or mount the larger source file before running this script."
        )

    adata = ad.read_h5ad(args.source_h5ad)

    if "counts" not in adata.layers:
        adata.layers["counts"] = adata.X.copy()

    sc.pp.filter_genes(adata, min_cells=args.min_cells)
    sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum=args.target_sum)
    sc.pp.log1p(adata)
    sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(
        adata,
        n_top_genes=args.n_top_genes,
        flavor=args.hvg_flavor,
        layer="counts",
        subset=False,
    )

    if "highly_variable" not in adata.var:
        raise RuntimeError("HVG selection did not create adata.var['highly_variable'].")

    adata_hvg = adata[:, adata.var["highly_variable"].to_numpy()].copy()

    args.out_h5ad.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.cogaps_input_h5ad.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.config_json.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    adata_hvg.write_h5ad(args.out_h5ad)

    cogaps_input = build_cogaps_input(adata_hvg)
    cogaps_input.write_h5ad(args.cogaps_input_h5ad)

    config = {
        "raw_h5ad": args.source_h5ad.name,
        "min_cells": args.min_cells,
        "target_sum": args.target_sum,
        "hvg_flavor": args.hvg_flavor,
        "n_top_genes": args.n_top_genes,
        "created_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat(),
        "prepared_h5ad": str(args.out_h5ad),
        "cogaps_input_h5ad": str(args.cogaps_input_h5ad),
    }
    args.config_json.write_text(json.dumps(config, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"Wrote prepared PBMC dataset: {args.out_h5ad}")
    print(f"Wrote CoGAPS input: {args.cogaps_input_h5ad}")
    print(f"Wrote preprocessing record: {args.config_json}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
````

````{.r code-copy="true"}
  if (length(x) != length(y) || length(x) < 2) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  if (sd(x) == 0 || sd(y) == 0) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  suppressWarnings(cor(x, y))
}

top_index_overlap <- function(current, final, n = 15) {
  n <- min(n, length(current), length(final))
  current_top <- names(sort(current, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(n)]
  final_top <- names(sort(final, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(n)]
  length(intersect(current_top, final_top)) / n
}

param_to_list <- function(params) {
  out <- list()
  for (nm in slotNames(params)) {
    value <- slot(params, nm)
    if (is.null(value)) {
      out[[nm]] <- NULL
    } else if (length(dim(value)) > 0) {
      out[[nm]] <- list(dim = dim(value), class = class(value))
    } else if (is.atomic(value) && length(value) <= 50) {
      out[[nm]] <- unname(value)
    } else {
      out[[nm]] <- list(class = class(value), length = length(value))
    }
  }
  out
}

build_trace_df <- function(md) {
  n <- max(length(md$chisq %||% numeric()), length(md$atomsA %||% numeric()), length(md$atomsP %||% numeric()))
  if (!is.finite(n) || n == 0) {
    return(data.frame())
  }
  fill <- function(x) {
    x <- x %||% numeric()
    c(as.numeric(x), rep(NA_real_, n - length(x)))
  }
  out <- data.frame(
    trace_index = seq_len(n),
    relative_progress = seq_len(n) / n,
    chisq = fill(md$chisq),
    atomsA = fill(md$atomsA),
    atomsP = fill(md$atomsP)
  )
  out$delta_chisq <- c(NA_real_, diff(out$chisq))
  out$delta_atomsA <- c(NA_real_, diff(out$atomsA))
  out$delta_atomsP <- c(NA_real_, diff(out$atomsP))
  out
}

summarize_snapshots <- function(snapshot_list, final_mat, phase, matrix_name, top_n) {
  if (!length(snapshot_list)) {
    return(data.frame())
  }
  final_vec <- as.numeric(final_mat)
  final_norm <- sqrt(sum(final_vec^2))
  do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(seq_along(snapshot_list), function(i) {
      snap <- snapshot_list[[i]]
      if (!is.null(colnames(snap))) {
        colnames(snap) <- canonicalize_pattern_names(colnames(snap))
      }
      snap_vec <- as.numeric(snap)
      overlap <- NA_real_
      if (identical(matrix_name, "A")) {
        per_pattern_overlap <- vapply(
          colnames(final_mat),
          function(pattern) top_index_overlap(snap[, pattern], final_mat[, pattern], n = top_n),
          numeric(1)
        )
        overlap <- mean(per_pattern_overlap)
      }
      data.frame(
        phase = phase,
        snapshot_label = names(snapshot_list)[i] %||% as.character(i),
        matrix = matrix_name,
        frobenius_to_final = sqrt(sum((snap_vec - final_vec)^2)),
        relative_frobenius_to_final = sqrt(sum((snap_vec - final_vec)^2)) / final_norm,
        correlation_to_final = safe_cor(snap_vec, final_vec),
        nnz = sum(snap_vec > 0),
        mean_top_overlap = overlap,
        row.names = NULL
      )
    })
  )
}

summarize_uncertainty <- function(A, P, A_sd, P_sd, top_n) {
  patterns <- colnames(A)
  do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(patterns, function(pattern) {
      ordered_genes <- order(A[, pattern], decreasing = TRUE)
      top_idx <- ordered_genes[seq_len(min(top_n, length(ordered_genes)))]
      weight_top <- A[top_idx, pattern]
      sd_top <- A_sd[top_idx, pattern]
      cv_top <- sd_top / pmax(abs(weight_top), 1e-8)
      data.frame(
        pattern = pattern,
        mean_loading_sd = mean(A_sd[, pattern]),
        median_loading_sd = median(A_sd[, pattern]),
        max_loading_sd = max(A_sd[, pattern]),
        mean_factor_sd = mean(P_sd[, pattern]),
        median_factor_sd = median(P_sd[, pattern]),
        max_factor_sd = max(P_sd[, pattern]),
        top_gene_mean_weight = mean(weight_top),
        top_gene_mean_loading_sd = mean(sd_top),
        top_gene_median_loading_cv = median(cv_top),
        row.names = NULL
      )
    })
  )
}
````

````{.python code-copy="true"}
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
cogaps_run_one_singleprocess.py

Run ONE CoGAPS job (single-process) for a given (K, seed, n_iter) using a cached
genes×cells input matrix.

Key fixes vs earlier version
----------------------------
1) The cache-skip logic now only skips when metrics.status == "ok".
   If a previous run failed, re-running the same job will try again automatically.

2) IFN/condition correlation no longer *requires* 'condition' in cogaps_input.var.
   If missing, it falls back to loading the preprocessed cells file from:
       outdir/cache/preprocessed_cells_*.h5ad
   and aligns by cell IDs.

Usage (typical)
---------------
python cogaps_run_one_singleprocess.py \
  --cogaps-input-h5ad results_cogaps_singleprocess_hpc/cache/cogaps_input_genesxcells_hvg3000_float64.h5ad \
  --outdir results_cogaps_singleprocess_hpc \
  --k 7 --seed 1 --n-iter 2000 \
  --use-sparse-opt \
  --cogaps-threads 1

Notes
-----
- Keep this "single-process" by NOT setting the 'distributed' parameter at all.
- Control BLAS threads via --blas-threads (important on HPC).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
import json
import time
import argparse
import traceback
import warnings
import os
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", message=r"Importing .* from `anndata` is deprecated.*", category=FutureWarning)

from PyCoGAPS.parameters import CoParams, setParams
from PyCoGAPS.pycogaps_main import CoGAPS

if str(SCRIPT_DIR) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(SCRIPT_DIR))

    atomic_write_h5ad,

    setup_logger,

    top_genes_table,

def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--cogaps-input-h5ad", required=True, help="Cached genes×cells AnnData (dense float64)")
    ap.add_argument("--outdir", default="results_cogaps_singleprocess_hpc", help="Output dir containing runs/ logs/ cache/")
    ap.add_argument("--k", type=int, required=True, help="Number of patterns (K)")
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--n-iter", type=int, required=True)

    ap.add_argument("--blas-threads", type=int, default=1, help="BLAS/OpenMP threads (important on HPC)")
    ap.add_argument("--cogaps-threads", type=int, default=1, help="Threads passed to CoGAPS(nThreads=...)")
    ap.add_argument("--use-sparse-opt", action="store_true", help="Use sparseOptimization / useSparseOptimization")
    ap.add_argument("--no-sparse-opt", action="store_true", help="Disable sparse optimization")
    ap.add_argument("--output-frequency", type=int, default=1000, help="How often CoGAPS prints trace updates")
    ap.add_argument("--checkpoint-interval", type=int, default=0, help="Checkpoint interval (0 disables checkpoints)")
    ap.add_argument("--checkpoint-out-file", type=str, default="", help="Optional checkpoint output file")
    ap.add_argument("--checkpoint-in-file", type=str, default="", help="Optional checkpoint input file")
    ap.add_argument("--n-snapshots", type=int, default=0, help="Snapshots per phase (0 disables snapshots)")
    ap.add_argument("--snapshot-phase", type=str, default="sampling", choices=["sampling", "equilibration", "all"], help="Which phase(s) to snapshot")
    ap.add_argument("--take-pump-samples", action="store_true", help="Enable pump statistics collection")
    ap.add_argument("--asynchronous-updates", action="store_true", help="Request asynchronous updates when CoGAPS threads > 1")
    ap.add_argument("--preprocessed-h5ad", type=str, default="", help="Optional processed cells x genes H5AD for condition alignment fallback")
    ap.add_argument("--force-rerun", action="store_true", help="Re-run even if metrics exist and status==ok")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    outdir = Path(args.outdir)
    runs_dir = outdir / "runs"
    logs_dir = outdir / "logs"
    runs_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    logs_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    tag = f"K{args.k}_seed{args.seed}_iter{args.n_iter}"
    run_log = logs_dir / f"run_{tag}.log"
    logger = setup_logger(run_log)

    set_blas_threads(args.blas_threads)

    result_path = runs_dir / f"cogaps_{tag}.h5ad"
    metrics_path = runs_dir / f"cogaps_{tag}.metrics.json"
    diagnostics_path = runs_dir / f"cogaps_{tag}.diagnostics.json"
    trace_path = runs_dir / f"cogaps_{tag}.trace.csv"
    top_genes_path = runs_dir / f"cogaps_{tag}.pattern_top_genes.csv"

    # Cache skip ONLY if status==ok
    if result_path.exists() and metrics_path.exists() and (not args.force_rerun):
        try:
            m = json.loads(metrics_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            if m.get("status") == "ok":
                logger.info(f"[CACHE] status=ok; skipping {tag}")
                logger.info(f"[CACHE] result:  {result_path}")
                logger.info(f"[CACHE] metrics: {metrics_path}")
                return
            else:
                logger.info(f"[CACHE] Found previous status={m.get('status')}; re-running {tag}")
        except Exception:
            logger.info("[CACHE] Could not parse metrics; re-running.")

    # If previous partial result exists, keep it for debugging but avoid mixing with new writes
    # (Atomic write will overwrite cleanly at the end.)
    t0 = time.time()
    status = "ok"
    err_txt = None
    ifn_pattern = None
    ifn_corr = None
    top_genes = None
    preprocessed_h5ad = Path(args.preprocessed_h5ad) if args.preprocessed_h5ad else None

    try:
        cogaps_input = ad.read_h5ad(args.cogaps_input_h5ad)

        params = CoParams(adata=cogaps_input)

        # IMPORTANT: do NOT set 'distributed' at all (keep single-process).
        sparse_opt = True
        if args.no_sparse_opt:
            sparse_opt = False
        elif args.use_sparse_opt:
            sparse_opt = True

        setParams(
            params,
            {
                "nPatterns": int(args.k),
                "nIterations": int(args.n_iter),
                "seed": int(args.seed),
                "useSparseOptimization": bool(sparse_opt),
                "takePumpSamples": bool(args.take_pump_samples),
            },
        )

        logger.info(
            "[RUN] Starting %s | sparse_opt=%s | blas_threads=%s | cogaps_threads=%s | "
            "output_frequency=%s | checkpoint_interval=%s | n_snapshots=%s | snapshot_phase=%s | pump=%s",
            tag,
            sparse_opt,
            args.blas_threads,
            args.cogaps_threads,
            args.output_frequency,
            args.checkpoint_interval,
            args.n_snapshots,
            args.snapshot_phase,
            args.take_pump_samples,
        )
        result = CoGAPS(
            cogaps_input,
            params,
            nThreads=int(args.cogaps_threads),
            outputFrequency=int(args.output_frequency),
            checkpointOutFile=args.checkpoint_out_file,
            checkpointInterval=int(args.checkpoint_interval),
            checkpointInFile=args.checkpoint_in_file,
            asynchronousUpdates=(True if args.asynchronous_updates else None),
            nSnapshots=int(args.n_snapshots),
            snapshotPhase=args.snapshot_phase,
        )

        logger.info(f"[INFO] Writing result: {result_path}")
        atomic_write_h5ad(result, result_path)

        ifn_pattern, ifn_corr, top_genes = compute_ifn_pattern(
            result=result,
            cogaps_input=cogaps_input,
            preprocessed_cells_h5ad=preprocessed_h5ad,
            outdir=outdir,
            top_n=int(args.top_genes),
            stim_label=args.stim_label,
        )
        logger.info(f"[METRICS] IFN pattern: {ifn_pattern} corr={ifn_corr:.3f}")
        logger.info(f"[METRICS] Top {args.top_genes} genes (first 10): {top_genes[:10]}")

    except Exception as e:
        status = "failed"
        err_txt = "".join(traceback.format_exception(type(e), e, e.__traceback__))
        logger.error("[ERROR] Run failed:\n" + err_txt)

    runtime = time.time() - t0
    diagnostics: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    payload = {
        "K": int(args.k),
        "seed": int(args.seed),
        "n_iter": int(args.n_iter),
        "status": status,
        "language": "Python",
        "package": "PyCoGAPS",
        "sparseOptimization": bool(False if args.no_sparse_opt else True),
        "outputFrequency": int(args.output_frequency),
        "checkpointInterval": int(args.checkpoint_interval),
        "nSnapshots": int(args.n_snapshots),
        "snapshotPhase": args.snapshot_phase,
        "takePumpSamples": bool(args.take_pump_samples),
        "asynchronousUpdates": bool(args.asynchronous_updates),
        "runtime_sec": float(runtime),
        "result_path": str(result_path),
        "metrics_path": str(metrics_path),
        "ifn_pattern": ifn_pattern,
        "ifn_corr": ifn_corr,
        "top_genes": top_genes,
        "error": err_txt,
        "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
    }
    if status == "ok" and result_path.exists():
        result_saved = ad.read_h5ad(result_path)
        diagnostics = summarize_result_uns(result_saved)
        atomic_write_json(diagnostics, diagnostics_path)
        trace_dataframe(result_saved).to_csv(trace_path, index=False)
        top_genes_table(result_saved, n_top=int(args.top_genes)).to_csv(top_genes_path, index=False)
        payload.update(diagnostics)

    atomic_write_json(payload, metrics_path)

    logger.info(f"[DONE] {tag} | {status.upper()} | {runtime/60:.2f} min | metrics: {metrics_path}")
    if status != "ok":
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
````

````{.python code-copy="true"}
from __future__ import annotations

"""Export lightweight Python/PyCoGAPS cooking-show artifacts.

The full selected Python `.h5ad` is a local-only input for this script. The
outputs written to `data/processed/selected_model_k6/python/` are the
GitHub/render-friendly artifacts used by the parallel Python tab when the full model object is not
present.
"""

from pathlib import Path
import os

import anndata as ad
import pandas as pd


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PREPROCESSED_H5AD = Path(
    os.environ.get(
        "COGAPS_PREPROCESSED_H5AD",
        ROOT / "data/processed/input/preprocessed_cells_hvg3000.h5ad",
    )
)
CHOSEN_RESULT_H5AD = Path(
    os.environ.get(
        "COGAPS_RESULT_H5AD",
        ROOT / "data/processed/selected_model_k6/python/cogaps_K6_seed2_iter2000.h5ad",
    )
)
OUT_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("COGAPS_OUT_DIR", ROOT / "data/processed/selected_model_k6/python"))

PATTERN_GENE_WEIGHTS_TSV_GZ = OUT_DIR / "pattern_gene_weights.tsv.gz"
PATTERN_CELL_ACTIVITIES_TSV_GZ = OUT_DIR / "pattern_cell_activities.tsv.gz"
PATTERN_CELL_ACTIVITIES_WITH_METADATA_CSV_GZ = OUT_DIR / "pattern_cell_activities_with_metadata.csv.gz"
PATTERN_TOP_GENES_CSV = OUT_DIR / "pattern_top_genes.csv"
PATTERN_CORRELATIONS_CSV = OUT_DIR / "pattern_correlations.csv"
PATTERN_ACTIVITY_BY_CELLTYPE_CONDITION_CSV = OUT_DIR / "pattern_activity_by_celltype_condition.csv"
PATTERN_ACTIVITY_BY_REPLICATE_CONDITION_CSV = OUT_DIR / "pattern_activity_by_replicate_condition.csv"
PATTERN_SUMMARY_CSV = OUT_DIR / "pattern_summary.csv"

STIM_LABEL = "stim"


def pattern_columns(df: pd.DataFrame) -> list[str]:
    return sorted(
        [c for c in df.columns if str(c).startswith("Pattern")],
        key=lambda value: int(str(value).replace("Pattern", "")),
    )


def top_genes_from_matrix(matrix: pd.DataFrame, pattern: str, n: int = 50) -> pd.DataFrame:
    top = matrix[pattern].sort_values(ascending=False).head(n)
    top_df = top.rename("weight").reset_index()
    top_df.columns = ["gene", "weight"]
    top_df.insert(0, "rank", range(1, len(top_df) + 1))
    top_df.insert(0, "pattern", pattern)
    return top_df


def main() -> None:
    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    adata_cells = ad.read_h5ad(PREPROCESSED_H5AD)
    result = ad.read_h5ad(CHOSEN_RESULT_H5AD)

    pattern_names = pattern_columns(result.obs)

    # In the saved CoGAPS result, genes live in obs and cells live in var.
    A = result.obs[pattern_names].copy()
    A.index.name = "gene"

    P = result.var[pattern_names].copy()
    P.index = result.var_names.astype(str)
    P.index.name = "cell_barcode"

    cell_meta_cols = [c for c in ["condition", "cell_type", "replicate", "label"] if c in adata_cells.obs.columns]
    cell_meta = adata_cells.obs.loc[P.index, cell_meta_cols].copy()
    cell_meta.index.name = "cell_barcode"

    if "X_umap" in adata_cells.obsm:
        umap = pd.DataFrame(
            adata_cells.obsm["X_umap"],
            index=adata_cells.obs_names.astype(str),
            columns=["umap_1", "umap_2"],
        )
        cell_meta = cell_meta.join(umap.loc[P.index], how="left")

    if "X_pca" in adata_cells.obsm:
        pca = pd.DataFrame(
            adata_cells.obsm["X_pca"][:, :2],
            index=adata_cells.obs_names.astype(str),
            columns=["pca_1", "pca_2"],
        )
        cell_meta = cell_meta.join(pca.loc[P.index], how="left")

    cell_activities_with_metadata = cell_meta.join(P, how="left").reset_index()

    stim_indicator = (cell_meta["condition"].astype(str) == STIM_LABEL).astype(int)
    pattern_corrs = (
        pd.Series(
            {pattern: P[pattern].corr(stim_indicator) for pattern in pattern_names},
            name="corr_with_stim",
        )
        .sort_values(ascending=False)
        .reset_index()
        .rename(columns={"index": "pattern"})
    )

    top_genes = pd.concat(
        [top_genes_from_matrix(A, pattern, n=50) for pattern in pattern_names],
        ignore_index=True,
    )

    activity_by_celltype_condition = pd.concat(
        [
            cell_activities_with_metadata
            .groupby(["cell_type", "condition"], observed=True)[pattern]
            .agg(["mean", "median", "count"])
            .reset_index()
            .rename(columns={"mean": "mean_activity", "median": "median_activity", "count": "n_cells"})
            .assign(pattern=pattern)
            for pattern in pattern_names
        ],
        ignore_index=True,
    )[
        ["pattern", "cell_type", "condition", "mean_activity", "median_activity", "n_cells"]
    ]

    activity_by_replicate_condition = pd.concat(
        [
            cell_activities_with_metadata
            .groupby(["replicate", "condition"], observed=True)[pattern]
            .agg(["mean", "median", "count"])
            .reset_index()
            .rename(columns={"mean": "mean_activity", "median": "median_activity", "count": "n_cells"})
            .assign(pattern=pattern)
            for pattern in pattern_names
        ],
        ignore_index=True,
    )[
        ["pattern", "replicate", "condition", "mean_activity", "median_activity", "n_cells"]
    ]

    pattern_summary_rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    corr_lookup = pattern_corrs.set_index("pattern")["corr_with_stim"]
    for pattern in pattern_names:
        top8 = ", ".join(top_genes.query("pattern == @pattern").head(8)["gene"].tolist())
        top15 = ", ".join(top_genes.query("pattern == @pattern").head(15)["gene"].tolist())
        dominant = (
            cell_activities_with_metadata
            .groupby("cell_type", observed=True)[pattern]
            .mean()
            .sort_values(ascending=False)
        )
        condition_means = (
            cell_activities_with_metadata
            .groupby("condition", observed=True)[pattern]
            .mean()
            .to_dict()
        )
        pattern_summary_rows.append(
            {
                "pattern": pattern,
                "corr_with_stim": float(corr_lookup[pattern]),
                "dominant_cell_type": dominant.index[0],
                "dominant_cell_type_mean_activity": float(dominant.iloc[0]),
                "mean_activity_ctrl": float(condition_means.get("ctrl", float("nan"))),
                "mean_activity_stim": float(condition_means.get("stim", float("nan"))),
                "top_genes_top8": top8,
                "top_genes_top15": top15,
            }
        )

    pattern_summary = pd.DataFrame(pattern_summary_rows).sort_values("corr_with_stim", ascending=False)

    A.reset_index().to_csv(PATTERN_GENE_WEIGHTS_TSV_GZ, sep="\t", index=False, compression="gzip")
    P.reset_index().to_csv(PATTERN_CELL_ACTIVITIES_TSV_GZ, sep="\t", index=False, compression="gzip")
    cell_activities_with_metadata.to_csv(PATTERN_CELL_ACTIVITIES_WITH_METADATA_CSV_GZ, index=False, compression="gzip")
    top_genes.to_csv(PATTERN_TOP_GENES_CSV, index=False)
    pattern_corrs.to_csv(PATTERN_CORRELATIONS_CSV, index=False)
    activity_by_celltype_condition.to_csv(PATTERN_ACTIVITY_BY_CELLTYPE_CONDITION_CSV, index=False)
    activity_by_replicate_condition.to_csv(PATTERN_ACTIVITY_BY_REPLICATE_CONDITION_CSV, index=False)
    pattern_summary.to_csv(PATTERN_SUMMARY_CSV, index=False)

    for path in [
        PATTERN_GENE_WEIGHTS_TSV_GZ,
        PATTERN_CELL_ACTIVITIES_TSV_GZ,
        PATTERN_CELL_ACTIVITIES_WITH_METADATA_CSV_GZ,
        PATTERN_TOP_GENES_CSV,
        PATTERN_CORRELATIONS_CSV,
        PATTERN_ACTIVITY_BY_CELLTYPE_CONDITION_CSV,
        PATTERN_ACTIVITY_BY_REPLICATE_CONDITION_CSV,
        PATTERN_SUMMARY_CSV,
    ]:
        size_mb = os.path.getsize(path) / (1024 * 1024)
        print(f"{path.name}: {size_mb:.2f} MB")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
````

````{.r code-copy="true"}
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(optparse)

`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (is.null(x)) y else x

lookup_count <- function(tbl, key) {

    as.integer(tbl[[key]])
  } else {

  }
}

script_arg <- grep("^--file=", commandArgs(trailingOnly = FALSE), value = TRUE)
script_path <- if (length(script_arg) > 0) sub("^--file=", "", script_arg[[1]]) else "."
ROOT <- normalizePath(file.path(dirname(script_path), ".."), winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
default_preprocessed <- file.path(ROOT, "data", "processed", "input", "preprocessed_cells_hvg3000.h5ad")
default_result_rds <- file.path(ROOT, "data", "processed", "selected_model_k6", "r", "cogaps_K6_seed2_iter2000.rds")

option_list <- list(
  make_option("--preprocessed-h5ad", type = "character", dest = "preprocessed_h5ad", default = default_preprocessed, help = "Processed cells x genes AnnData (.h5ad) [default %default]"),
  make_option("--result-rds", type = "character", dest = "result_rds", default = default_result_rds, help = "Saved CoGAPS R result (.rds) [default %default]"),
  make_option("--outdir", type = "character", default = default_out_dir, help = "Output directory [default %default]")
)

opt <- parse_args(OptionParser(option_list = option_list))

PREPROCESSED_H5AD <- opt$preprocessed_h5ad
CHOSEN_RESULT_RDS <- opt$result_rds
OUT_DIR <- opt$outdir

TOP_N_GENES <- 15
MIN_CELLS_PER_PSEUDOBULK <- 20
CPM_PSEUDOCOUNT <- 0.5
STRONG_ABS_LOG2FC <- 0.5
MODERATE_ABS_LOG2FC <- 0.25
HIGH_CONSISTENCY <- 0.75

pattern_columns <- function(x) {
  pats <- grep("^Pattern_?[0-9]+$", x, value = TRUE)
  pats[order(as.integer(sub("^Pattern_?", "", pats)))]
}

canonicalize_pattern_names <- function(x) {
  sub("^Pattern_?([0-9]+)$", "Pattern\\1", x)
}

ensure_pattern_matrix_orientation <- function(mat, expected_rows, expected_names) {
  if (nrow(mat) != expected_rows && ncol(mat) == expected_rows) {
    mat <- t(mat)
  }
  if (nrow(mat) != expected_rows) {
    stop(sprintf("Unexpected matrix shape. Expected %d rows, got %d.", expected_rows, nrow(mat)))
  }
  if (is.null(rownames(mat))) {
    rownames(mat) <- expected_names
  }
  mat
}

classify_direction <- function(mean_log2fc, sign_consistency, n_pairs) {
  if (is.na(mean_log2fc) || n_pairs == 0) {
    return(list(direction = "not_tested", evidence_strength = "insufficient_pairs"))
  }

  if (mean_log2fc > 0) {
    direction <- "up_in_stim"
  } else if (mean_log2fc < 0) {
    direction <- "down_in_stim"
  } else {
    direction <- "mixed_or_unclear"
  }

  abs_fc <- abs(mean_log2fc)
  if (abs_fc >= STRONG_ABS_LOG2FC && sign_consistency >= HIGH_CONSISTENCY) {
    strength <- "strong"
  } else if (abs_fc >= MODERATE_ABS_LOG2FC && sign_consistency >= 0.625) {
    strength <- "moderate"
  } else if (abs_fc < 0.1 || sign_consistency < 0.625) {
    strength <- "weak_or_mixed"
  } else {
    strength <- "suggestive"
  }

  if (identical(direction, "mixed_or_unclear")) {
    strength <- "weak_or_mixed"
  }

  list(direction = direction, evidence_strength = strength)
}

extract_top_pattern_genes <- function(A, top_n = 15) {
  do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(pattern_columns(colnames(A)), function(pattern) {
      ordered <- sort(A[, pattern], decreasing = TRUE)
      ordered <- head(ordered, top_n)
      data.frame(
        pattern = pattern,
        gene = names(ordered),
        rank = seq_along(ordered),
        cogaps_weight = unname(ordered),
        row.names = NULL
      )
    })
  )
}

get_counts_assay <- function(sce) {
  assay_names <- assayNames(sce)
  if ("counts" %in% assay_names) {
    return(assay(sce, "counts"))
  }
  if ("X" %in% assay_names) {
    warning("counts assay not found; falling back to X. Directionality is best interpreted when raw counts are available.")
    return(assay(sce, "X"))
  }
  stop("Could not find a counts or X assay in the preprocessed H5AD.")
}

sum_gene_counts <- function(mat, gene_idx, cell_idx) {
  block <- mat[gene_idx, cell_idx, drop = FALSE]
  if (inherits(block, "sparseMatrix")) {
    return(as.numeric(Matrix::rowSums(block)))
  }
  rowSums(as.matrix(block))
}

group_library_size <- function(mat, cell_idx) {
  block <- mat[, cell_idx, drop = FALSE]
  if (inherits(block, "sparseMatrix")) {
    return(as.numeric(sum(block)))
  }
  sum(as.matrix(block))
}

make_pseudobulk <- function(sce, genes, group_cols, min_cells) {
  counts_mat <- get_counts_assay(sce)
  gene_idx <- match(genes, rownames(sce))
  if (anyNA(gene_idx)) {
    stop("Some genes were not found in the processed SingleCellExperiment.")
  }

  obs <- as.data.frame(colData(sce))
  obs$.cell_index <- seq_len(ncol(sce))

  keys <- do.call(paste, c(obs[group_cols], sep = "\r"))
  groups <- split(seq_len(nrow(obs)), keys)

  rows <- list()
  row_i <- 1L
  for (idx in groups) {
    group_df <- obs[idx, , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(group_df) < min_cells) {
      next
    }

    cell_idx <- group_df$.cell_index
    gene_counts <- sum_gene_counts(counts_mat, gene_idx, cell_idx)
    row <- as.list(group_df[1, group_cols, drop = FALSE])
    row$n_cells <- nrow(group_df)
    row$library_size_total_counts <- group_library_size(counts_mat, cell_idx)
    row$library_size_pattern_genes <- sum(gene_counts)
    for (j in seq_along(genes)) {
      row[[genes[[j]]]] <- gene_counts[[j]]
    }
    rows[[row_i]] <- row
    row_i <- row_i + 1L
  }

  if (!length(rows)) {
    return(data.frame())
  }
  do.call(rbind.data.frame, c(rows, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
}

add_cpm <- function(pseudobulk, genes) {
  out <- pseudobulk
  for (gene in genes) {
    count_col <- if (gene %in% names(out)) gene else make.names(gene)
    if (!count_col %in% names(out)) {
      stop(sprintf("Could not find pseudobulk count column for gene '%s'.", gene))
    }
    out[[paste0(gene, "__cpm")]] <- ifelse(
      out$library_size_total_counts > 0,
      (out[[count_col]] / out$library_size_total_counts) * 1e6,
      0
    )
  }
  out
}

paired_directionality <- function(pseudobulk_cpm, genes, pair_cols, context_cols) {
  if (!nrow(pseudobulk_cpm)) {
    return(list(pair_df = data.frame(), summary_df = data.frame()))
  }

  split_keys <- do.call(paste, c(pseudobulk_cpm[pair_cols], sep = "\r"))
  grouped <- split(seq_len(nrow(pseudobulk_cpm)), split_keys)

  pair_rows <- list()
  pair_i <- 1L

  for (idx in grouped) {
    group <- pseudobulk_cpm[idx, , drop = FALSE]
    if (!all(c("ctrl", "stim") %in% group$condition)) {
      next
    }
    ctrl <- group[group$condition == "ctrl", , drop = FALSE][1, ]
    stim <- group[group$condition == "stim", , drop = FALSE][1, ]

    pair_info <- as.list(ctrl[1, pair_cols, drop = FALSE])
    for (gene in genes) {
      ctrl_cpm <- as.numeric(ctrl[[paste0(gene, "__cpm")]])
      stim_cpm <- as.numeric(stim[[paste0(gene, "__cpm")]])
      log2fc <- log2(stim_cpm + CPM_PSEUDOCOUNT) - log2(ctrl_cpm + CPM_PSEUDOCOUNT)
      pair_rows[[pair_i]] <- c(
        context_cols,
        pair_info,
        list(
          gene = gene,
          ctrl_cpm = ctrl_cpm,
          stim_cpm = stim_cpm,
          log2fc_stim_vs_ctrl = log2fc,
          ctrl_n_cells = as.integer(ctrl$n_cells),
          stim_n_cells = as.integer(stim$n_cells)
        )
      )
      pair_i <- pair_i + 1L
    }
  }

  if (!length(pair_rows)) {
    return(list(pair_df = data.frame(), summary_df = data.frame()))
  }

  pair_df <- do.call(rbind.data.frame, c(pair_rows, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
  numeric_cols <- c("ctrl_cpm", "stim_cpm", "log2fc_stim_vs_ctrl", "ctrl_n_cells", "stim_n_cells")
  for (col in numeric_cols) {
    pair_df[[col]] <- as.numeric(pair_df[[col]])
  }

  summary_group_cols <- unique(c("gene", setdiff(pair_cols, "replicate")))
  summary_keys <- do.call(paste, c(pair_df[summary_group_cols], sep = "\r"))
  summary_groups <- split(seq_len(nrow(pair_df)), summary_keys)

  summary_rows <- list()
  summary_i <- 1L

  for (idx in summary_groups) {
    gene_df <- pair_df[idx, , drop = FALSE]
    group_info <- as.list(gene_df[1, summary_group_cols, drop = FALSE])
    vals <- as.numeric(gene_df$log2fc_stim_vs_ctrl)
    vals <- vals[is.finite(vals)]
    if (!length(vals)) {
      next
    }
    mean_log2fc <- mean(vals)
    median_log2fc <- median(vals)
    n_pairs <- length(vals)
    n_up <- sum(vals > 0)
    n_down <- sum(vals < 0)
    n_zero <- sum(vals == 0)
    sign_consistency <- max(n_up, n_down, n_zero) / n_pairs
    direction <- classify_direction(mean_log2fc, sign_consistency, n_pairs)
    pvalue <- if (n_pairs >= 2 && !all(abs(vals) < .Machine$double.eps)) {
      tryCatch(wilcox.test(vals, mu = 0, alternative = "two.sided", exact = FALSE)$p.value, error = function(e) NA_real_)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }

    summary_rows[[summary_i]] <- c(
      context_cols,
      group_info,
      list(
        mean_log2fc_stim_vs_ctrl = mean_log2fc,
        median_log2fc_stim_vs_ctrl = median_log2fc,
        n_pairs = n_pairs,
        n_up_pairs = n_up,
        n_down_pairs = n_down,
        n_zero_pairs = n_zero,
        sign_consistency = sign_consistency,
        wilcoxon_pvalue = pvalue,
        direction = direction$direction,
        evidence_strength = direction$evidence_strength
      )
    )
    summary_i <- summary_i + 1L
  }

  summary_df <- do.call(rbind.data.frame, c(summary_rows, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
  numeric_summary_cols <- c(
    "mean_log2fc_stim_vs_ctrl", "median_log2fc_stim_vs_ctrl", "n_pairs", "n_up_pairs",
    "n_down_pairs", "n_zero_pairs", "sign_consistency", "wilcoxon_pvalue"
  )
  for (col in numeric_summary_cols) {
    summary_df[[col]] <- as.numeric(summary_df[[col]])
  }
  summary_df$wilcoxon_fdr <- p.adjust(summary_df$wilcoxon_pvalue, method = "BH")

  list(pair_df = pair_df, summary_df = summary_df)
}

make_pattern_direction_summary <- function(global_summary) {
  do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(split(global_summary, global_summary$pattern), function(df) {
      direction_counts <- table(df$direction)

      up_genes <- head(df$gene[df$direction == "up_in_stim"][order(df$mean_log2fc_stim_vs_ctrl[df$direction == "up_in_stim"], decreasing = TRUE)], 5)

        row.names = NULL
      )
    })
  )
}
````
